all_found.desc: [BUG] existingAncestor accepts a work directory that exists but cannot be entered (no search permission); git cannot run there, so ownership lookup fails and mine() attributes the run to the main checkout. A linked worktree loses its abandoned-run blocker when the run's work dir is inaccessible.

[BUG] Rows of collided ids are skipped, but the legacy-ledger.size stamp is still written at the end of the pass; since fsm commands never append to the legacy ledger its size is unchanged, so after the collision is resolved and MigrateLegacyRuns moves the run, MigrateLegacyRows returns early at the stamp check and never copies that run's terminal row. A migrated run is left permanently without its ledger row, silently.

rejected.desc: [BUG] MigrateLegacyRows copies the legacy ledger row of an id that MigrateLegacyRuns left behind as a collision (the store already holds a different run under that id but no terminal row yet). record.Exists then sees the id, the live run's own terminal write can hit id_conflict (different HeadSHA/WorkflowHash), and the copied FSMRunDir names the wrong run.

[BUG] The Toplevel-error fallback after a successful StoreDir is never exercised (a work dir inside .git itself), so the repository's every-statement coverage gate fails for internal/status (99.8%). CI's coverage gate fails the PR.

findings.consequence: A still-running store run of that id later has its terminal row refused; needs a user-chosen --run-id collision, and was already possible before whenever the legacy ledger grew.
findings.issue: If a collision is resolved by deleting the legacy copy of the run (keeping the store's run), the next unstamped pass copies the discarded run's stale legacy row under the store's run id; nothing ties a legacy row to whether its run directory was moved.
